_command_shape.size_handling: fontFactory.cpp:144-146: size = Utility::strToDouble(sizeValue) * fontFactor, and if the product is 0 the size becomes 12. Utility::strToDouble returns 0 on an unparsable or empty string (utility.cpp:399-406), so omitting `size` gives a 12-point font that is NOT multiplied by the resolution factor fontFactor (fontFactory.cpp:86).

_acceptance_test.source: src/appModule/fontFactory.cpp:141-169 (lookup at :149-153); the accepted set is the std::map m_strToTarget filled in FontFactory::setStrToTarget, src/appModule/fontFactory.cpp:41-53
_acceptance_test.case_sensitive_evidence: fontFactory.cpp:149 is m_strToTarget.find(targetName) on a std::map<std::string, CLASSEFONT> (declared fontFactory.hpp:115) with the default std::less<std::string>, i.e. a plain byte comparison. Neither commandFont (app_command_interface.cpp:4278-4313) nor updateFont applies any case folding to the target, unlike the `size` and `align` keys of the `text` command which are explicitly upper-cased (app_command_interface.cpp:2825, 2828). So "Text" or "STARS" are rejected.
_acceptance_test.on_unknown: Silent-to-the-script no-op with a log line: fontFactory.cpp:150-153 writes "Unknown FontFactory target " + targetName at LOG_TYPE::L_WARNING (fontFactory.cpp:151) and returns. No exception, no assert, no abort. updateFont returns void and commandFont does not test anything after calling it (app_command_interface.cpp:4302-4304), so debug_message stays empty and the `font` command reports SUCCESS to the script for a misspelt target. A wrong target name is therefore invisible in the script and visible only in the engine log.
_acceptance_test.differs_from_TF_list: no - the accepted set is EXACTLY the ten TF_* spellings. setStrToTarget (fontFactory.cpp:43-52) inserts exactly the ten macros TF_TEXT, TF_PLANETS, TF_CONSTELLATIONS, TF_CARDINAL, TF_STARS, TF_MENU, TF_NEBULAE, TF_GRIDS, TF_LINES, TF_DISPLAYS (base_command_interface.hpp:684-693), one entry each, and setStrToTarget is the only writer of m_strToTarget (it is called only from the constructor, fontFactory.cpp:38). The family check for `font` can be armed as a closed, case-sensitive, exactly-ten-member set.
_acceptance_test.cross_check: core.cpp:1594-1603 calls updateFont with nine literal targets (text, menu, planets, constellations, cardinal_points, grids, lines, displays, stars) at every sky-locale change; the tenth, "nebulae", is at core.cpp:1603. All ten literals are in the accepted set, and no literal outside the TF_* list appears.
notes: Naming inversion worth knowing: TF_TEXT ("text") maps to CLASSEFONT::CLASS_MENU and TF_MENU ("menu") maps to CLASSEFONT::CLASS_UI (fontFactory.cpp:43 and :48). CLASS_MENU is the Media/TextMgr font, not a menu font. Reading the enumerator name instead of the map will give the wrong answer for both targets.

CLASS_MENU is the only accepted target that is not in listFont: it is special-cased and returns early at fontFactory.cpp:156-159 via media->updateTextFont. The other nine are pushed into listFont by FontFactory::init (fontFactory.cpp:91-131).

The assert(0) at fontFactory.cpp:167 fires only if an accepted target resolves to a CLASSEFONT absent from listFont; after a normal init() that cannot happen for any of the ten, so it is dead code on the `font` command path.
The `font` command surface also has the target-free form `font action initial`, which rebuilds every font at its startup size and name (fontFactory.cpp:196-200) and never consults the accepted set.

names.name: text
names.doc: The typeface used for the text a script puts on the dome with the 'text' command.
names.source: spelling TF_TEXT base_command_interface.hpp:684; mapped to CLASSEFONT::CLASS_MENU at fontFactory.cpp:43; handled by the early-return branch fontFactory.cpp:156-159 -> media.hpp:362-364 -> TextMgr::updateFont text_mgr.cpp:216-222; the text itself is created by the `text` command, app_command_interface.cpp:2813-2837, and drawn by TextMgr::draw text_mgr.cpp:207-214
names.notes: Side effect a script author will see: TextMgr::updateFont calls clearCache() and clear() (text_mgr.cpp:218-219), and clear() empties textUsr (text_mgr.cpp:136-139) - so changing this font ERASES every text currently on the dome. TextMgr keeps seven sizes around the requested one (mFontSize+2*(i-3), text_mgr.cpp:220-221), which is what the `text` command's size words select. Despite the enumerator being called CLASS_MENU this is the script-text font, not the menu font.

_suspected_bugs.what: FontFactory::updateAllFont dereferences a past-the-end list iterator for the "text" target
_suspected_bugs.source: src/appModule/fontFactory.cpp:171-180, specifically the find_if at :176 and the dereference at :177
_suspected_bugs.detail: updateAllFont walks every entry of m_strToTarget and, for each, searches listFont for a FontContener with that CLASSEFONT. CLASS_MENU (the "text" target, fontFactory.cpp:43) is never pushed into listFont - FontFactory::init pushes only the other nine (fontFactory.cpp:91-131) - so find_if returns listFont.end() and line 177 evaluates it2->fontPtr->getFontSize() on the end iterator. m_strToTarget is a std::map ordered by string, so "text" is the last key visited and the undefined behaviour lands at the very end of the loop.
_suspected_bugs.when_reachable: core.cpp:1590 and core.cpp:1592 - updateAllFont is called whenever the sky locale is switched to one starting with "zh" or "ja". The else branch (core.cpp:1594-1603) avoids it by calling updateFont per target, which is why the ordinary locales do not hit it.

_suspected_bugs.what: A misspelt `font target` is reported to the script as a success
_suspected_bugs.detail: updateFont returns void after logging a warning, and commandFont neither checks nor sets debug_message afterwards, so the script's status is the same as for a target that worked. This is exactly the gap an editor-side family check closes.

_suspected_bugs.what: W_SIZE is defined twice with the same replacement text
_suspected_bugs.detail: Both expand to "size", so the redefinition is legal and harmless, but it means the `font` command's size key and another command's size key are two macros away from diverging silently.
